text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto said she did not aspire to return to power or work as opposition leader in the National Assembly. She urged her party to choose another leader.
- Shahid Hamid, former defence and law minister in the caretaker government, took over as governor of Punjab province.
- The economic minister of Pakistan's embassy in Brussels said anti-dumping duties on Pakistani textile products may not be imposed by the European Union for lack of evidence.
- Pakistan's trade gap in the first eight months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) remained almost static compared to the corresponding period in 1995/96.
- The wheat harvest in southern Sindh province is due to start next week.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government has shelved a plan to merge state-run National Investment Trust and the Investment Corporation of Pakistan, sources said.
- The Economic Coordination Committee of the cabinet has decided to analyse the trade balance to find ways to increase exports and reduce the trade deficit.
- A leading broker at the Karachi Stock Exchange has been accused of involvement in the sale of fake shares worth 80 million rupees, sources said.
- Karachi will get an extra 540 megawatts of electricity in 1997 when three private power plants come on line.
THE NATION
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif agreed to withdraw police powers from Rangers in the southern port city of Karachi.
- The International Monetary Fund has asked Pakistan to explain the sharp decline in revenue collection targets.
THE FRONTIER POST
- Interior Minister Shujaat Hussain ruled out a ban on militant religious organisations.
- General Moinuddin Haider is likely to be appointed as new Governor of Sindh province.
- Pakistan has been able to bring down opium poppy cultivation to an all-time low of 1,000 hectares.
- The government will promulgate an ordinance to ban floor-crossing in the national and provincial assemblies.
